question: Why do sinusoidal implicit neural representations sometimes collapse to a zero output on high-frequency-dominant signals, and can target-aware noise in the initial weights prevent that failure without adding parameters?

key_findings.claim: The paper identifies a spectral bottleneck in which SIREN's activation and empirical-NTK energy remain concentrated at low frequencies, preventing even nominally representable high-frequency modes from learning.
key_findings.evidence: For high-frequency synthetic and natural audio, the NTK-weighted spectral energy does not move toward target modes, error fails to decay, and output collapses to zero; the same 13.4 dB zero-output failure is reported for WIRE, FINER, HOSC, and Gaussian activations under the tested setup.

anchors.section: III.A-B Challenges and Learning Dynamics in Fourier Space

key_findings.claim: WINNER broadens frequency support by adding Gaussian perturbations to weights before the first two hidden layers while leaving the trained parameter count unchanged.
key_findings.evidence: The added noise increases pre-activation variance by the derived factor sqrt(1+d s^2/2), which the paper interprets as an effective activation-frequency scaling; its effect propagates through later layers and changes the empirical NTK eigenbasis.

key_findings.claim: The target-aware noise rule is an empirically fitted heuristic rather than a derived optimum.
key_findings.evidence: Noise scales use the target spectral centroid in one exponential and one linear formula; the authors explicitly say the form is ad hoc, selected from experiments, and requires a more principled derivation.

anchors.section: IV.A Target-aware Specification of Noise Scales

key_findings.claim: SIREN2 produces large fitting gains on high-frequency audio and selected images, but it is not uniformly best against newer INR architectures.
key_findings.evidence: Audio experiments report SIREN2 above 60 dB on difficult clips and strong gains over SIREN. On images it improves SIREN by 7% to 69%, yet FINER is higher on camera, castle, 2D Riemann, and Kodak rows, while SIREN2 leads on several texture averages and noisy-image metrics.

anchors.section: Tables II-III Image fitting and denoising

key_findings.claim: Improved initialization also helps audio denoising and inpainting, though gains can be small or reverse on low-frequency cases.
key_findings.evidence: At 5 dB input SNR, SIREN2 slightly or materially exceeds FINER++ across four clips; inpainting improves most tested sparsities, but at 50% retained samples on bach.wav SIREN is marginally better (46.89 versus 46.81 dB).

anchors.section: Tables IV-V Audio denoising and inpainting

method.core_idea: Treat initialization as a controllable spectral prior and match its activation/NTK support to the target before optimization begins.
method.mechanism: Diagnose spectral collapse through layerwise activation FFTs and empirical-NTK eigenmodes; compute a target spectral centroid; use it to set two Gaussian perturbation scales for the first two weight matrices; then retain the ordinary SIREN training procedure.
assumptions: The target spectrum is known or can be estimated
Spectral centroid is sufficient to choose useful perturbation scales
Layer-one activations are approximately arcsine distributed for the variance argument
A learning-rate decay schedule is available to control oscillatory training

techniques.role: Tracks layerwise pre/post-activation power spectra to localize a learning bottleneck.
Weights Fourier content by empirical NTK eigenvalues to connect initialization with mode-wise error decay.
Perturbs the first two weight matrices according to a target-spectrum heuristic without adding trainable parameters.

evaluations.result: SIREN2 consistently improves high-frequency-dominant clips and reports values above 60 dB on several signals
evaluations.baseline: SIREN, Gaussian activation, WIRE, and FINER

evaluations.metric: PSNR, SSIM, MAE, LPIPS, and DISTS
evaluations.result: large gains over SIREN and strongest or comparable denoising, but FINER wins multiple clean-fitting rows
evaluations.baseline: SIREN, ReLU positional encoding, WIRE, FINER, and Gaussian activation

evaluations.setting: Audio denoising at 5 dB SNR and sparse audio inpainting
evaluations.result: usually improves FINER++ or SIREN, with one small reversal at high retained fraction
evaluations.baseline: FINER++ for denoising and SIREN for inpainting

limitations: Author-stated: target spectral knowledge is required, which is unavailable in denoising and many PDE settings.
Author-stated: performance remains sensitive to learning rate and its decay schedule.
Author-stated: the spectral-centroid-to-noise mapping is ad hoc.
Reviewer inference: extensive per-task scale searches complicate claims that the heuristic removes expensive tuning.
failure_modes: Broadening the spectrum can suppress low-frequency reconstruction or amplify observation noise.
A single centroid cannot distinguish multimodal spectra with the same mean frequency.
Perturbations that help fitting may destabilize gradient flow without a tuned scheduler.
Unknown target spectra make the initialization circular in inverse problems.
reusable_insights: Audit what frequency modes the optimization kernel can learn, not only what the architecture can represent.
A no-parameter initialization change can alter effective NTK bandwidth.
Report exceptions where spectral broadening hurts low-frequency or high-sparsity regimes.
open_questions: Can noise scales be learned online without looking at ground truth?
Can a multi-band statistic replace the lossy spectral centroid?
Does spectral support at initialization predict convergence under feature-learning rather than NTK-like dynamics?

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Neural Representations with Periodic Activation Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: SIREN introduces sinusoidal activations and a variance-stabilizing initialization; the reviewed paper identifies a high-frequency collapse under that initialization and perturbs its weights based on target spectrum.

competitive_landscape.title: FINER: Flexible spectral-bias tuning in Implicit NEural Representation by Variable-periodic Activation Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: FINER tunes supported frequencies through variable-periodic activations and bias ranges; WINNER retains SIREN's activation and perturbs early weights to reshape pre-activation and NTK spectra.

competitive_landscape.title: Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains
competitive_landscape.difference: Fourier features explicitly map coordinates into a tunable stationary-kernel basis; WINNER tries to obtain comparable bandwidth control through initialization without the embedding's parameter and feature expansion.

competitive_landscape.title: WIRE: Wavelet Implicit Neural Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: WIRE uses complex Gabor-wavelet activations for localized space-frequency bias; WINNER keeps periodic SIREN activations and alters only initial weights, with stronger audio fitting in the reviewed experiments but mixed image comparisons.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: WINNER is a target-aware noisy initialization that prevents a newly characterized spectral bottleneck in SIRENs and improves audio fitting without extra parameters.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper connects activation spectra, empirical-NTK eigenmodes, a variance calculation, and broad cross-modal experiments.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The spectral-collapse diagnosis is valuable, but spectral-bias control is already central to Fourier features, FINER, and WIRE; the distinct contribution is early-weight noise plus an empirical target-centroid rule, whose circularity and tuning burden remain unresolved.

reviewer_notes: Read all 16 extracted pages, including result tables and explicit limitations. Primary arXiv records were checked on 2026-08-23; comparisons distinguish target-matched rows from broad state-of-the-art language.
